description: Scheduler features: weekly auto-draft (sendWeeklyPlan cron) and self-reflection engine (checkAndSendObservation). Both live in server/scheduler.js. Both are non-blocking — failures must not crash the scheduler. Depends on FEAT-001 completing first (life_anchors table must exist).
steps:
Step 1 — server/scheduler.js: Add sendWeeklyPlan() function. Pattern matches existing sendWeeklyDigest(). Structure:
  1. const owner = await db.prepare('SELECT id, telegram_chat_id FROM users WHERE is_owner = TRUE LIMIT 1').get() — for SQLite compat use: WHERE is_owner = 1 OR is_owner = TRUE (use a helper that checks both: (db.USE_PG ? 'TRUE' : '1')). Actually use: WHERE is_owner = ' + (db.USE_PG ? 'TRUE' : '1') + ' LIMIT 1'.
  2. If !owner || !owner.telegram_chat_id, return early.
  3. Fetch anchors: SELECT * FROM life_anchors WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY day_of_week ASC NULLS LAST, date ASC NULLS LAST — use owner.id.
  4. Fetch top 5 open tasks ordered by priority: SELECT title, priority FROM tasks WHERE user_id = ? AND status = 'open' ORDER BY CASE priority WHEN 'high' THEN 0 WHEN 'normal' THEN 1 WHEN 'low' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END ASC LIMIT 5 — use owner.id.
  5. Compute week range: Mon DD to Sun DD. Use JS Date: today is Sunday (cron fires Sunday); Mon = today+1 day, Sun = today+7 days. Format as 'Mon DD' using toLocaleDateString with weekday:short, day:numeric.
  6. Build message string:
     '📅 week ahead — [Mon DD] to [Sun DD]\n\n'
     + (anchors.length ? 'ANCHORED:\n' + anchorLines + '\n\n' : '')
     + 'OPEN TASKS (top 5):\n' + taskLines
     + (aiLine ? '\n\n💡 ' + aiLine : '')
  7. Anchor line format — day_of_week → 3-letter day name; start_time–end_time — anchor title. For one_off, use the date field.
  8. Task line format: priority === 'high' ? '🔴' : priority === 'low' ? '🟢' : '🟡', then title.
  9. AI suggestion (non-blocking try/catch): getProviderPlan() → fetchWithProviderFallback with a prompt asking for one sentence week-framing suggestion based on the anchor + task data, max 15 words. Wrap in try/catch, skip on failure.
  10. Send via sendMessage(message, owner.id) — sendMessage is already imported from telegram.
  11. Wrap entire function body in try/catch, console.error on failure.

Step 2 — server/scheduler.js: Add checkAndSendObservation(userId) function. Called non-blocking from sendMorningBrief after the owner's brief is sent (see step 3). Structure:
  Observation A — completion rate: SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM tasks WHERE user_id = ? AND created_at >= [30 days ago]; SELECT COUNT(*) as done FROM tasks WHERE user_id = ? AND status = 'done' AND created_at >= [30 days ago]. If total >= 5 and done/total < 0.30: obsA = '🪞 Vis noticed: you\'ve completed less than 30% of tasks created in the last 30 days — want to clear the backlog together?'
  Observation B — finance net: compute last 3 calendar months (month boundaries in JS). For each month query: SELECT type, SUM(amount) as total FROM finance_entries WHERE user_id = ? AND COALESCE(imported_date, created_at) >= ? AND COALESCE(imported_date, created_at) < ? AND category != 'transfers' GROUP BY type. If all 3 months have negative net: obsB = '🪞 Vis noticed: your finances have been net-negative three months in a row — might be worth a look.'
  Observation C — stagnant high-priority tasks: SELECT title FROM tasks WHERE user_id = ? AND status = 'open' AND priority = 'high' AND last_touched_at <= [7 days ago]. If any: obsC = '🪞 Vis noticed: ' + count + ' high-priority task(s) haven\'t been touched in 7+ days — ' + titles joined by ', '.
  Priority: C > B > A. Send the highest-priority applicable observation via notifyUser(userId, obs) (notifyUser is already defined in scheduler.js). Wrap everything in try/catch, console.error on failure, never throw.

Step 3 — server/scheduler.js: Hook checkAndSendObservation into sendMorningBrief. Inside the per-user for loop, after the existing `await notifyUser(userId, message.trim(), 'Morning brief');` line, check if the user is the owner (is_owner flag): const ownerRow = await db.prepare('SELECT is_owner FROM users WHERE id = ?').get(userId); if (ownerRow?.is_owner === true || ownerRow?.is_owner === 1) { checkAndSendObservation(userId).catch(e => console.error('[scheduler] reflection failed:', e.message)); }  — note the non-blocking pattern: no await, .catch() to suppress crashes.

Step 4 — server/scheduler.js: Register sendWeeklyPlan in startScheduler(). Add: cron.schedule('0 16 * * 0', sendWeeklyPlan);  after the existing sendWeeklyDigest line. Also add sendWeeklyPlan and checkAndSendObservation to module.exports.

Step 5 — server/scheduler.js: Add import at top (or inline inside function). getProviderPlan and fetchWithProviderFallback are already required inside sendMorningBrief inline (const { getProviderPlan, fetchWithProviderFallback } = require('./ai-providers')). Use the same inline require pattern inside sendWeeklyPlan for consistency. sendMessage is already imported at the top of scheduler.js.
acceptance_criteria: node server/index.js starts without errors and logs '[scheduler] running'
sendWeeklyPlan() can be called directly without crashing: node -e "require('./server/scheduler').sendWeeklyPlan().catch(console.error)"
checkAndSendObservation can be exported and called without crashing
startScheduler registers the '0 16 * * 0' cron (visible via cron.getTasks() or by reading the source)
sendMorningBrief completes without error for opted-in users — checkAndSendObservation fires non-blocking for the owner
verification: node server/index.js — confirm '[scheduler] running' in console with no errors

node -e "const s=require('./server/scheduler'); s.sendWeeklyPlan().then(()=>console.log('sendWeeklyPlan ok')).catch(e=>console.error('FAIL',e.message))" — should print 'sendWeeklyPlan ok' (or skip silently if no owner/telegram configured)
node -e "const s=require('./server/scheduler'); s.sendMorningBrief().then(()=>console.log('morning brief ok')).catch(e=>console.error('FAIL',e.message))" — should complete without crashing
